key_value_text.quote: Three independent electron neutrino searches are performed across multiple single electron final states ... the results are found to be consistent with the nominal electron neutrino rate expectations from the Booster Neutrino Beam and no excess of electron neutrino events is observed.
key_value_text.value: Three independent electron-neutrino searches (exclusive 1-proton, semi-inclusive pion-less, fully inclusive) all consistent with nominal νe rate expectations from the BNB; no excess of electron neutrino events observed in any of the three

name: Search for an Excess of Electron Neutrino Interactions in MicroBooNE Using Multiple Final State Topologies
notes: MicroBooNE was built specifically to test the MiniBooNE low-energy excess (result:miniboone-low-energy-excess-2021) using a technology that can distinguish electrons from photons; this 2021 multi-topology search found no corresponding excess.

significance.locator: arXiv:2110.14054, abstract (no significance/sigma reported for a null result)
significance.note: This is a null/consistency result across three independent analyses; the abstract reports consistency with background rather than a single sigma value.

summary.plain: MicroBooNE, built to check MiniBooNE's mysterious excess with a detector that can tell electrons from photons, looked three different ways and found nothing unusual: the electron-neutrino rate matched expectations every time.
summary.technical: Using three independent electron-neutrino selections (exclusive two-body 1p, semi-inclusive pionless, fully inclusive), MicroBooNE finds no excess of electron neutrino interactions above the standard-model expectation from the Booster Neutrino Beam, disfavoring a simple electron-like-excess interpretation of the MiniBooNE anomaly.

title: Search for an Excess of Electron Neutrino Interactions in MicroBooNE Using Multiple Final State Topologies
why_it_matters: This was MicroBooNE's primary physics goal: using liquid-argon imaging to determine whether MiniBooNE's excess was made of electrons (as a sterile-neutrino oscillation would produce) or something else. Finding no excess in any of three independent, differently-systematic analyses disfavors simple electron-flavor explanations of the anomaly.
